newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude rises late session on Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude rises late session on Iraq news.

text.p: NYMEX crude jumped late session Thursday on a report that U.N. oil monitors were arrested by a Kurdish faction in northern Iraq, although U.N. officials in Iraq said they had no knowledge of the arrests.

"I think there is some concern, and it may be premature, that Saddam's possible antics may jeapordize the future of the oil-for-food sales," said Thomas Blakeslee, analyst with Cargill Investor Services in New York.
The news jolted crude from its lacklustre trade, and it pushed it up 25 cents to $19.97 a barrel after it stagnated between $19.70 and $19.80 most of the day.
U.N. officials in Baghdad have no knowledge of United Nations oil monitors being arrested in northern Iraq, as reported Thursday by the BBC monitoring service.

The BBC report, quoting the Iraqi Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) radio said six U.N. envoys monitoring the distribution of fuel in northern Iraq disappeared this week in areas under the control of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP).
The United Nations said definitive word on the situation in northern Iraq would come Friday morning when U.N. officers in Baghdad return to work.
The KDP, a rival of the PUK, joined with Saddam Hussein's troops to attack PUK regions in August in northern Iraq and detained the implementation of the oil-for-food deal between the U.N. and Iraq.
The accord received final approval in December, but now dealers speculated about Hussein's connection to the KDP's alleged involvement in the arrests.
May heating oil was up 0.30 cent at 55.95 cents a gallon while May gasoline rose 1.16 cents at 62.90 cents a gallon.
